body.speaker: The Prophet Muhammad
body.text_en: I seek Allah's refuge from knowledge that is of no benefit.

body.speaker: The Prophet Muhammad
body.text_en: A servant's preoccupation with useless matters is a sign that Allah has withdrawn His special favor from him. And if even a single moment of a servant's life passes in pursuit of something other than that for which Allah created him, then that is a matter of profound sorrow.

body.speaker: The Prophet Muhammad
body.text_en: An individual whose condition, even after forty years of age, is such that the good within him does not prevail over the evil, should prepare to go to Hell.

body.speaker: The Prophet Muhammad
body.text_en: On the Day of Judgment, the most severe torment will be visited upon the scholar whom Allah did not benefit through his knowledge — that is, one who did not act upon what he acquired.

body.speaker: Shaykh Junaid Baghdadi
body.text_en: All discourses and spiritual signs turned out to be of no avail. But certain cycles of prayer I had performed during the Tahajjud were of benefit.

body.speaker: Imam al-Ghazali
body.text_en: Do not deprive yourself of good deeds, do not neglect the knowledge of outward matters, and do not be without inner excellences and noble qualities of the heart. Be firmly convinced that knowledge alone, without righteous deeds, will not benefit you on the Day of Judgment.

body.speaker: Hasan al-Basri
body.text_en: I remembered the plea of the inhabitants of Hell when they will beseech the inhabitants of Paradise to pour upon them even a little water.

body.speaker: Shaykh Sufyan al-Thawri
body.text_en: Allah the Exalted has created a wind that blows in the last part of the night. At that hour, the voices of those servants of Allah who engage in His remembrance and seek His forgiveness are carried by this wind and presented to the Court of Allah the Exalted.

body.speaker: Luqman
body.text_en: My son! Do not let the rooster prove more intelligent than you. Let it not be that he rises in the last part of the night to proclaim the hour of remembrance and glorifies his Lord, while you remain sunk in the deep sleep of heedlessness, carelessness, and negligence.
But as for the one who has stood in awe of his Sustainer's Presence and restrained his inner self from base and evil desires, Paradise will be the place of rest.
All that is with you is bound to come to an end, whereas all that which is with Allah is everlasting.
Verily, the noblest of you in the sight of Allah is the one who is most deeply conscious — most fearful — of Him.
It is We who distribute their means of livelihood — their sustenance — among them in the life of this world.
Verily, Shaytan is your enemy, so treat him as your enemy.
And there is no living creature on earth whose sustenance is not the responsibility of Allah.

body.speaker: Hatim ibn Ism
body.text_en: I looked at the people of this world and saw that everyone has a beloved. Yet these beloveds — some accompany their lovers only until the illness that brings death, some until death itself, and some until the grave. After burial, all the loved ones return. None descend into the grave to dwell with the deceased, to offer companionship in the darkness, solitude, narrowness, and terror of that place.

body.speaker: Hatim ibn Ism
body.text_en: After reaching this awareness and determination, I made my righteous deeds my beloved.

body.speaker: Shaykh Shafeeq
body.text_en: Bravo, O Hatim. You have said a most excellent thing.

body.speaker: Hatim ibn Ism
body.text_en: I glanced at the people and saw that everyone was running after the pleasures and desires of the Nafs (the lower self that incites one toward evil) and was subservient to its desires.

body.speaker: Hatim ibn Ism
body.text_en: I developed the certitude that the Wise Quran is correct. I then took a firm stand against my Nafs and was resolved to oppose it. I disciplined it to such a degree that I refused to fulfil any of its desires, until at last it began to find peace and satisfaction in the worship of Allah, the Exalted.

body.speaker: Hatim ibn Ism
body.text_en: I saw that every person, through great pain and hard labour, was busy accumulating the possessions of this mortal world — money, wealth, goods — and was greatly pleased to have amassed much of it.

body.speaker: Hatim ibn Ism
body.text_en: Therefore whatever material possessions I had accumulated in this world, I spent entirely in the Way of Allah by distributing them among pious indigents and the needy, so that those possessions would be deposited with Allah as my trust, and would become a source of immense good and ransom — salvation — in the life hereafter.

body.speaker: Hatim ibn Ism
body.text_en: I looked at the people and saw that some believe grandeur and honour belong to the nation or tribe that is large and powerful; some believe it comes from abundance of wealth, possessions, family, and relatives; some believe it lies in displaying anger, in beating and killing and pillage; some believe it lies in wasteful spending — and so they take pride and boast in their respective fictions.

body.speaker: Hatim ibn Ism
body.text_en: This alone is correct; this alone is the truth. The thoughts of the people of the world are false conjectures. Therefore I adopted Taqwa (pious reverence, consciousness, awe, and fear of Allah), so that I might be counted among those of the highest rank in the sight of Allah.

body.speaker: Hatim ibn Ism
body.text_en: I looked at the people complaining against one another. I found that they were doing this on account of envy, jealousy, and enmity, and that the root cause was competition over greatness, grandeur, possessions, wealth, and knowledge.

body.speaker: Hatim ibn Ism
body.text_en: I reflected that Allah has appointed all possessions and ranks from the beginning of creation; no one has any control or say in this matter. Therefore I ceased to compete with or harbour jealousy toward anyone, and I remained content with Allah's distribution and with His appointed destiny, living in peace with all of creation by surrendering every jealousy and enmity against the creatures of God.

body.speaker: Hatim ibn Ism
body.text_en: I saw that every person holds enmity toward someone else for some reason.

body.speaker: Hatim ibn Ism
body.text_en: From that time forward, I regarded Satan alone as my enemy and refused to obey any of his promptings. Instead, I cultivated obedience to Allah, followed His commandments, and devoted myself entirely to His worship and servitude.

body.speaker: Hatim ibn Ism
body.text_en: I saw that every person is preoccupied with his or her livelihood and the search for sustenance, consumed by intense effort in that pursuit. In this race, many do not even distinguish between the Halal (what is permissible) and the Haram (what is forbidden), and instead degrade themselves by pursuing doubtful and forbidden earnings.

body.speaker: Hatim ibn Ism
body.text_en: I am also among those living creatures of God present upon the earth. Therefore I devoted myself to the worship of Allah and held firm to the certitude that He would bring my sustenance to

body.speaker: Imam al-Ghazali
body.text_en: Of these eight admonitions, there are four things you must do and four things you must not do — so that your knowledge does not turn against you on the Day of Judgment.

body.speaker: Ghazali
body.text_en: As far as possible, do not engage in religious debates with everyone, and do not argue with anyone on any matter — religious or otherwise — for there are many hidden harms within such disputes, and the harms far outweigh any benefits.

body.speaker: Ghazali
body.text_en: ostentation and show — Riya (performing the religious act for human applause rather than for Allah) — jealousy, arrogance, resentment, enmity, pride, and egotism.

body.speaker: Ghazali
body.text_en: Asking questions about religious and spiritual matters is like describing the diseases of the heart and their causes before a physician of the heart. And the efforts of that physician to cure those diseases are like the responses to the questions raised.

body.speaker: Ghazali
body.text_en: Whatever answer you give, no matter how sound, such a person will regard you as an enemy, and the fire of envy within them will only burn more fiercely.

body.speaker: Prophet 'Isa (Jesus)
body.text_en: with the permission of God — not incapable of restoring the dead to life, yet he was incapable of curing the fool and the ignorant.

body.speaker: Ghazali
body.text_en: who has spent only a brief time acquiring knowledge, has not even begun to grasp intellectual and transmitted religious learning, and yet raises objections against scholars who have devoted their entire lives to those very disciplines. The depth of knowledge and insight possessed by a great scholar is entirely beyond their comprehension. That incomprehension itself is their foolishness.

body.speaker: Ghazali
body.text_en: Whatever question this person asks, or whatever objection they raise, arises not from jealousy, fault-finding, or the desire to test, but from an earnest search for truth and correct guidance. This is the patient who can be cured. To answer the questions of such a person is therefore not merely permissible — it is obligatory (Wajib — religiously required).

body.speaker: Allah
body.text_en: O Son of Mary! First admonish your own soul (Nafs); then, if it accepts your counsel, admonish others — otherwise have shame before Me.
